concepts.name: Reaction rate meaning
concepts.summary: State that reaction rate is the change in concentration of a reactant or product per unit time.

concepts.name: Collision theory
concepts.summary: Explain that reactions occur when particles collide with sufficient energy and proper orientation.

concepts.name: Factors affecting rate
concepts.summary: Describe how concentration, temperature, surface area and catalysts change reaction rate and why.

concepts.name: Activation energy
concepts.summary: Understand activation energy as the minimum energy needed for a collision to lead to reaction.

concepts.name: Reversible reactions
concepts.summary: Recognise that some reactions proceed in both directions and are written with a double arrow.

concepts.name: Dynamic equilibrium
concepts.summary: Explain that at equilibrium forward and reverse rates are equal and concentrations stay constant while reactions continue.

concepts.name: Le Chatelier's principle
concepts.summary: State qualitatively that a system at equilibrium responds to a disturbance by partly counteracting it.

misconceptions.text: At equilibrium the reaction has stopped.
At equilibrium the concentrations of reactants and products are equal.
A catalyst makes a reaction go faster because it adds energy to the molecules.

concepts.name: Average and instantaneous rate
concepts.summary: Calculate average rates from data and estimate instantaneous rates from the slope of a concentration-time curve.

concepts.name: Rate law and rate constant
concepts.summary: Write a rate law of the form rate = k[A]^m[B]^n and identify the roles of k and the orders.

concepts.name: Reaction order from data
concepts.summary: Determine orders and k from initial-rate experiments.

concepts.name: Equilibrium constant expression
concepts.summary: Write Kc and Kp expressions from balanced equations, omitting pure solids and liquids.

concepts.name: Magnitude of K
concepts.summary: Interpret large and small K values as favouring products or reactants at equilibrium.

concepts.name: Reaction quotient comparison
concepts.summary: Compute Q and compare it with K to predict the direction a reaction proceeds.

concepts.name: Applying Le Chatelier shifts
concepts.summary: Predict shifts from changes in concentration, pressure, volume and temperature.

misconceptions.text: Reaction orders can be read directly from the coefficients of the balanced equation.
A large K means the reaction is fast.
Adding a catalyst or a pure solid shifts the equilibrium position.

concepts.name: Integrated rate laws
concepts.summary: Use zero-, first- and second-order integrated laws to find concentrations and times.

concepts.name: Half-life analysis
concepts.summary: Relate half-life to k and order, and recognise when it is concentration independent.

concepts.name: Graphical order determination
concepts.summary: Analyse plots of [A], ln[A] and 1/[A] against time to identify order and k.

concepts.name: Arrhenius equation
concepts.summary: Use the Arrhenius equation and its linear form to relate k, temperature and activation energy.

concepts.name: ICE table calculations
concepts.summary: Set up initial, change and equilibrium quantities to solve for unknown equilibrium concentrations.

concepts.name: Approximation validity
concepts.summary: Judge when x can be neglected and when a quadratic must be solved.

concepts.name: K manipulation and Kp-Kc
concepts.summary: Adjust K for reversed, scaled or summed reactions and convert between Kc and Kp using Δn.

concepts.name: Thermodynamic link to K
concepts.summary: Relate K to ΔG° and explain how temperature changes K according to ΔH°.

misconceptions.text: Half-life is constant for every reaction regardless of order.
Changing temperature shifts equilibrium but leaves K unchanged.
The small-x approximation is always valid when K is small, regardless of initial concentration.

concepts.name: Elementary steps and molecularity
concepts.summary: Distinguish elementary steps from overall reactions and derive rate laws for elementary steps from molecularity.

concepts.name: Rate-determining step analysis
concepts.summary: Analyse a mechanism to derive a rate law consistent with its slowest step.

concepts.name: Steady-state and pre-equilibrium
concepts.summary: Apply pre-equilibrium and steady-state approximations to eliminate intermediates from rate laws.

concepts.name: Evaluating proposed mechanisms
concepts.summary: Judge whether a mechanism fits stoichiometry and observed rate law, recognising that data cannot prove it.

concepts.name: Catalysis and energy profiles
concepts.summary: Interpret reaction profiles to show catalysts lower barriers of both directions without changing K.

concepts.name: Simultaneous equilibria
concepts.summary: Analyse systems with multiple coupled equilibria, such as solubility with complexation or acid-base buffers.

concepts.name: Kinetic versus thermodynamic control
concepts.summary: Evaluate how rates and stabilities determine product distributions under different conditions.

misconceptions.text: The rate law of a multistep reaction follows from its overall stoichiometry.
A rate law matching experiment proves the proposed mechanism is correct.
A catalyst increases the equilibrium yield of products.

concepts.name: Design of kinetic experiments
concepts.summary: Design experiments such as isolation and flooding to separate orders and minimise confounding effects.

concepts.name: Error analysis in kinetic fits
concepts.summary: Evaluate uncertainty in k and Ea from linear and nonlinear fits and judge model adequacy.

concepts.name: Transition state theory
concepts.summary: Evaluate rate behaviour using activation enthalpy and entropy and compare with Arrhenius and collision models.

concepts.name: Complex kinetic schemes
concepts.summary: Build and solve models of consecutive, parallel and reversible-approach reactions, including numerical solution.

concepts.name: Enzyme and surface catalysis models
concepts.summary: Evaluate saturation kinetics models and their limiting rate behaviours.

concepts.name: Relaxation and perturbation methods
concepts.summary: Judge how perturbation techniques measure fast kinetics and extract rate constants from relaxation to equilibrium.

concepts.name: Detailed balance and microscopic reversibility
concepts.summary: Use detailed balance to link forward and reverse rate constants to K and test mechanisms for consistency.

concepts.name: Nonideal and open systems
concepts.summary: Design treatments using activities, fugacities and steady flow where ideal concentration-based K and batch assumptions fail.

misconceptions.text: Thermodynamic K alone tells you how quickly a system approaches equilibrium.
Activation energy from an Arrhenius plot is a fixed property valid across any temperature range and mechanism change.
Equilibrium constants defined with concentrations remain exact at high ionic strength or pressure.
